races.title: State House, District 30
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Marcia Morey
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 30 (Durham County) since April 2017. Former 14th Judicial District assistant district attorney, district court judge (1999–2017) and chief district court judge (2011–2017). Former executive director of the Governor's Commission on Juvenile Crime and Justice. 1976 Olympic swimmer.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions by Morey on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on institutional or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, abortion restrictions, or school vouchers. Her campaign site lists "Healthcare & Reproductive Freedom" and "Public Safety & Gun Laws" as priority issues, but the text behind those headings was not available. Her birth year is on Wikipedia, but no source gave her exact year of arrival in North Carolina. The list of bills she sponsored on Ballotpedia was empty in the page we read. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages reviewed. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys for 2020–2026.

local.label: Roots 55: She was born and raised in Decatur, Illinois, and the record shows her working in Durham as an assistant district attorney by 1994 and serving as a Durham-area judge from 1999 to 2017, so she has lived in North Carolina as an adult for more than 25 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State House member since 2017 (appointed April 5, 2017, then re-elected). Before that she was a district court judge for 18 years, chief district court judge for 5 years, an assistant district attorney, and executive director of the Governor's Commission on Juvenile Crime and Justice. She holds a J.D. from Northwestern University.
qual.why: About nine years of legislative service, plus a long law and justice-policy career as a prosecutor, judge and state commission director, place her in the high band for writing law and budgets.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says that in the House she has focused her energy on reforming gun safety laws. It does not name specific measures.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site criticizes Republican policy for "prioritizing private schools over public schools" and says she has worked on investing in public schools. It names no specific voucher or teacher-pay measure.

cands.name: Ray Ubinger
cands.bio: Ray Ubinger is a Libertarian Party candidate who ran for the North Carolina House of Representatives, District 30, in 2026. He was also the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 22 in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024. No elected office is documented.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Ray Ubinger was born or raised, when he moved to North Carolina, or his occupation and education. He did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, and no campaign platform, interview or questionnaire was available. We found no documented stance on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing, and no endorsements, controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Ballotpedia lists only repeated Libertarian candidacies for the state legislature (Senate District 22 in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024; House District 30 in 2026), all lost. It lists no occupation or office held.
qual.why: His occupation and work history could not be found, so no score is given.
